slides.title: Axonex AI Group Joins FLAIR’s Embodied AI International Applications Hub and Launches Education Humanoid TOMO
slides.highlight: Axonex AI Group has joined FLAIR’s Embodied AI International Applications Hub and launched an education humanoid named TOMO, highlighting the growing industry focus on embodied AI for learning applications.

slides.title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
slides.tldr: LLM-LLM DEBATE FRAMEWORK FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This study introduces a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework to analyze how conversational influence and opinion dynamics vary across model combinations, providing insights relevant to modeling agent interactions in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: LLM opinion dynamics are model-dependent; same-model pairs converge while cross-model pairs diverge.
card.key_idea: Controlled LLM-LLM debates track bidirectional opinion shifts, revealing that convergence depends on model pairing rather than persuasion instructions.
card.evaluation: 480 debates using GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite; measured via self-reported positions and in-dialogue interaction states.
card.limitation: Findings are specific to two models and one topic; explicit manipulation instructions showed no consistent effect across pairings.

slides.title: Model Capacity Frontier: A Development Framework for LLM-Supported Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces the Model Capacity Frontier framework to systematically navigate configuration sensitivity in LLM-supported agent-based models, directly addressing the design challenges in MIMIC's goal of simulating harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Introduces Model Capacity Frontier to distinguish architectural limits from configuration errors in LLM-supported social simulations.
card.key_idea: Characterizes attainable empirical performance via Pareto frontiers across admissible configurations, guiding iterative architectural refinement.
card.evaluation: Validated on 12,000-agent crowd simulation using video-derived metrics for temporal, spatial, and flow errors across two event instances.
card.limitation: Frontier estimation is computationally expensive for LLMs, requiring sparse sampling that may miss optimal configurations or overfit noise.

slides.title: The Butterfly Effect in LLM Social Simulations: From Architecture Sensitivity to Robustness Audits
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates how minor implementation changes in LLM agents can drastically alter collective social simulation outcomes, introducing TRAILS as a framework for auditing robustness in multi-agent systems.

card.one_liner: LLM social simulations are highly sensitive to implementation choices, requiring robustness audits to validate scientific claims.
card.key_idea: Analyzes how representation and design perturbations propagate through multi-agent interactions, introducing TRAILS for systematic robustness auditing.
card.evaluation: Tested on Prisoner's Dilemma and echo chambers across four LLMs; persona changes shifted cooperation by 75.2pp, showing model-dependent amplification.
card.limitation: Findings limited to two specific regimes and fixed horizons; robustness does not guarantee empirical validity or human behavioral correspondence.

slides.title: Gossip Agents: Reputation through Opinion Dynamics over Evolving Networks
slides.highlight: This paper explores how reputation information propagates through dynamic communication networks using opinion dynamics, a mechanism relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies at the meso-scale.

card.one_liner: Reputation diffusion via gossip over dynamic networks promotes cooperation and sustainability in multi-agent social dilemmas.
card.key_idea: Agents form private opinions via DeGroot dynamics over evolving networks, with a tunable broadcast radius controlling reputation reach.
card.evaluation: Tested on n-player Prisoner's Dilemma and Harvest using DQN; compared against no-reputation baselines across varying broadcast radii.
card.limitation: Relies on fixed, hand-engineered assessment rules for prosocial/antisocial behavior, which may not generalize to complex environments.

slides.title: Beyond Small Talk: Modeling Disclosure Trajectories in Human-AI Conversation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Trajectory-based Disclosure Evaluation (TraDE), a framework grounded in Social Penetration Theory to assess how preceding disclosure history shapes AI behavior. It is relevant to HyECHO for modeling the temporal dynamics of engagement and social norms in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: TraDE framework reveals AI responses depend on disclosure history, not just current depth.
card.key_idea: Controlled evaluation varying prior disclosure trajectories while holding current depth constant to isolate history effects.
card.evaluation: Tested 4-8 models on AnthroBench/INTIMA/ELEPHANT; compared against ESConv human baselines using DTW matching.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic persona generation and specific depth definitions, potentially limiting ecological validity.

slides.title: JR West Unveils Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: JR West's introduction of humanoid robots highlights the growing integration of embodied agents in public service settings, a domain relevant to research on human-robot interaction and social robotics.

slides.title: Whose Polarization Is It? Auditing Fairness in Network Polarization Measures
slides.tldr: AUDITING BIAS IN NETWORK POLARIZATION METRICS
slides.highlight: This work reveals that standard network polarization measures systematically bias minority groups, a critical consideration for HyECHO's modeling of group norms and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams where subgroups may be embedded in larger networks.

card.one_liner: Polarization measures unfairly inflate minority scores due to surrounding majority structure and opinion dynamics.
card.key_idea: Audits fairness via measurement invariance and structural exogeneity, introducing Network-Weighted Distance to fill coverage gaps.
card.evaluation: Synthetic sweeps, diagnostic topologies, and real-world political networks; no measure passes all checks, with minorities systematically over-scored.
card.limitation: Findings rely on the assumption that majority-induced opinion changes constitute a fairness violation rather than legitimate social influence.

slides.title: Tairex Launches Multi-Agent AI System for Clinical Collaboration
slides.highlight: Tairex has launched a multi-agent AI system designed to enhance clinical collaboration and decision support, offering a relevant case study in coordinating autonomous agents for complex decision-making tasks.

slides.title: Discovery-Probability Graph Planning for Embodied Agents in Tasks with Hidden Cooperation Requirements
slides.highlight: This work addresses hidden-cooperation tasks where the need for collaboration is only revealed through interaction, proposing a graph-based planning method to optimize information exchange and action efficiency. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction by providing a framework for agents to autonomously discover and manage cooperative dynamics in uncertain environments.

card.one_liner: DPGP enables embodied agents to coordinate on hidden-cooperation tasks via probabilistic discovery graphs.
card.key_idea: Encodes target count/location uncertainty in a discovery-probability graph, updated by observations, to minimize expected costs via joint search.
card.evaluation: Tested on HiddenCoop (C-WAH/TDW-MAT); DPGP achieved 99.3%/58.3% cooperative success, beating baselines with lower latency and token usage.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-derived semantic priors for initialization, which may lack empirical calibration in complex or novel environments.

slides.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
slides.highlight: This work introduces market-based post-training for decentralized agent swarms, enabling joint learning of action policies and self-orchestration without central coordination, which aligns with MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies through scalable agent interactions.

card.one_liner: Market-based post-training enables decentralized agent swarms to jointly learn action policies and self-orchestration through bidding.
card.key_idea: Agents submit bids to determine who acts; these bids also dictate credit assignment, coupling participation decisions with policy learning.
card.evaluation: Tested on embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research; outperforms monolithic RL and fixed orchestration baselines on rewards and accuracy.
card.limitation: Requires counterfactual rollouts for bidding updates, potentially increasing training compute; relies on verified rewards and specific role specializations.

slides.title: The Weight of Teamwork: Does Communication Structure Help LLM Scientists Search for Scientific Laws?
slides.highlight: This study examines how communication structures and selection rules impact LLM team performance in scientific search tasks, offering insights relevant to modeling hybrid human-AI team dynamics and collective decision-making processes.

card.one_liner: Separating candidate generation from selection reveals that communication structure rankings depend on the final delivery rule.
card.key_idea: Evaluates LLM teams in symbolic regression by isolating peer visibility/update timing from selection rules, showing architecture gaps shift with delivery mechanisms.
card.evaluation: LLM-SRBench (Qwen/Terra); fixed budgets; metrics: held-out Q-score, bootstrap CIs; compares Independent, Ring, Star, Complete under shared/alternative selectors.
card.limitation: Specific to symbolic regression; does not identify communication mechanisms or universally preferred topologies; results may not generalize to broader scientific discovery.

slides.title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
slides.tldr: CONVERGENCE GUARANTEES FOR LLM AGENT COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This paper formalizes LLM agent collaboration as block optimization with proven convergence guarantees, offering a theoretical foundation for understanding how hybrid human-AI teams coordinate local actions to achieve global objectives.

card.one_liner: Formalizes LLM agent collaboration as block optimization with linear convergence guarantees and empirical validation.
card.key_idea: Agents optimize local blocks with global corrections; a coordinator verifies proposals and merges non-interfering or compatible combinations.
card.evaluation: Tested on robot routing (GPT-OSS-120B), SQLite, and synthetic tasks; shows faster convergence than single agents and validates theoretical bounds.
card.limitation: Requires accurate global corrections and assumes block error bounds; performance depends on how well local proposals combine without interference.

slides.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a sparse-pose-driven interface that decouples high-level task intent from whole-body coordination, offering a potential architectural insight for improving the locomotion and manipulation capabilities of embodied social robots like Haru.

card.one_liner: SP-HLM combines sparse body poses with a learned motion prior for efficient humanoid loco-manipulation.
card.key_idea: Integrates explicit five-point pose targets with an implicit latent motion prior via a VLA, motion generator, and tracker.
card.evaluation: Tested on 8 simulated and 4 real-world tasks; outperforms joint/token baselines with 52.75% success and lower tracking errors.
card.limitation: Hand control is limited to simple finger joint targets, restricting complex dexterous manipulation capabilities.
